layers.note: A tufted herb of open subalpine forest, ridges and meadow edges.

moisture.note: Moderately dry to moist, well-drained ground.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; abundant on open slopes.

elevation_m.note: Sea level on the coast to about 2,300 m in the Cascades.

shade_tolerance.note: Sun to part shade under open conifers.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −12 to 4 °C; gone below −20 °C and above 8 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −35 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −42 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 9 to 20 °C; gone below 6 °C, where summers are too short, and above 24 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 900 to 4,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 500.

degree_days_5.note: About 250 to 2,200 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 100.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.4, gone by 0.25.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.5 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.7.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Beargrass grows from British Columbia to California and east to Montana and Wyoming (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
